original_question: Suppose that U is a nonprincipal ultrafilter on ω, and B is a group such that every element b ∈ B belongs to a subgroup of B that is a homomorphic image of Z^ω/U. Must B then be a homomorphic image of an ultraproduct group(∏_{i∈ω} G_i)/U for some groups G_i? This is Question 19 in(G. M. Bergman, Pacific J. Math., 274(2015), 451–495). An affirmative answer would imply that every torsion group was such a homomorphic image for every U, and so would give positive answers to both parts of 21.11.
target_in_paper: Problem 21.12 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)" of The Kourovka Notebook, which explicitly identifies itself as Bergman's Question 19; in the current arXiv version it is annotated with a negative solution.
correct_elements: The draft already captures essentially all of the official mathematical content of 21.12. It correctly fixes a nonprincipal ultrafilter U on ω, states the local hypothesis on each element of B via a subgroup of B that is a homomorphic image of ℤ^ω/U, asks whether B must itself be a homomorphic image of a countable ultraproduct (∏_{i∈ω} G_i)/U, and accurately reproduces the notebook's contextual remark that a positive answer would imply positive answers to both parts of 21.11.
missing_details: State explicitly that ω is the index set of natural numbers.
Define ℤ^ω/U as the ultrapower of the additive group ℤ modulo the fixed ultrafilter U.
Define (∏_{i∈ω} G_i)/U as the ultraproduct with respect to that same ultrafilter U.

Spell out the local hypothesis in elementwise form: for each b∈B there exists a homomorphism φ_b: ℤ^ω/U → B whose image contains b; equivalently, there exists a subgroup H_b≤B with b∈H_b and H_b a homomorphic image of ℤ^ω/U.
Make explicit that B and the groups G_i are arbitrary groups; no abelian assumption is imposed on them.

If the 21.11 remark is retained, separate it from the core question, since it is motivation/context rather than part of the hypothesis or conclusion. For a stand-alone formulation, it is cleaner to omit that cross-reference.
refined_question: Let U be a fixed nonprincipal ultrafilter on ω, and write ℤ^ω/U for the corresponding ultrapower of the additive group ℤ. Suppose B is a group such that for every b∈B there exists a homomorphism φ_b: ℤ^ω/U → B whose image contains b (equivalently, b lies in a subgroup H_b≤B that is a homomorphic image of ℤ^ω/U). Must there exist groups G_i, indexed by i∈ω, such that B is a homomorphic image of the U-ultraproduct (∏_{i∈ω} G_i)/U?
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of Kourovka Problem 21.12, and that is the narrow target to preserve. The only real deficiencies are that the ultrapower/ultraproduct notation is left implicit, the local hypothesis should be stated in a fully stand-alone way, and the 21.11 sentence is motivational rather than part of the mathematical problem. I therefore keep the scope exactly at the fixed-ultrafilter, elementwise local-image hypothesis and the conclusion asking for a countable U-ultraproduct surjecting onto B, without broadening it. The current arXiv version of the notebook also notes that the answer is negative.
